observation.visible_scene: A close-up of a clear glass jar filled with transparent liquid, suspended vertically down its center by a string that is encrusted with a column of white, jagged crystals (a crystallization growth on a wick). A horizontal line of foam/bubbles sits at the liquid surface, and a thin bed of loose granular crystals rests on the jar floor. Out-of-focus white fairy lights on twisted wire frame the scene on the left and right against a dark background.
visible_changes: The crystal-coated string column slowly thickens over the segment: the spiky crystal teeth along its edges, particularly on the right side and the lower half, become slightly more pronounced and extended from the first to the last frame.
The bed of loose crystals at the bottom of the jar gains a few more scattered granular grains, especially toward the lower left and right, indicating continued deposition.
A small detached crystal flake suspended in the liquid to the left of the column stays roughly stationary relative to the column throughout the excerpt (no clear independent drift).
The foam/bubble line at the surface persists, with only minor internal rearrangement of bubbles.
The jar and the background bulbs appear marginally larger by the end, consistent with a very slow camera zoom-in or approach (not certain).
outside_clip_unknowns: The start and end of the crystallization process lie outside this crop; growth is already underway at t=0 and continues past t=2.67s.
The identity of the solution, the string material, and the long-term outcome of the crystal column are not shown.
Whether the bottom accumulation reflects net growth or merely lighting/reflection changes cannot be confirmed from these frames alone.
uncertain_details: Camera motion: the slight enlargement of the jar and background lights could be a slow zoom-in or could be a static shot with depth-of-field/lighting variation; background evidence is limited.
The exact degree of crystal thickening is subtle and partly confounded by focus and specular highlights on the wet crystals.
